Decision: Whether to use AI at all
UK: Each body applies the test to itself
EU: The deployer decides; some practices are banned (Art. 5)

Decision: Whether a tool counts as high-risk
UK: No legal category; each body judges
EU: Provider assesses the conditional Article 6(3) exception, documents its assessment and meets registration duties (Art. 6(4)); authority scrutiny remains.

UK: Internal, plus central spend approvals; ICO consultation where data-protection risk remains
EU: Police biometric identification, authorised independently; EDPS consultation for EU institutions; third-party conformity assessment of some systems before market (Art. 43(1))

UK: Named in guidance rather than binding rules (UK174, UK071, UK268, AI_Insights)
EU: The deployer must suspend use if it has reason to consider a risk (Art. 26(5)); authorities can order withdrawal or recall (Art. 79(2))

Decision: What to measure, and the pass mark
UK: Bodies choose purpose-appropriate measures within applicable duties; the Playbook asks for objective measures and UK071 offers illustrative thresholds and testing methods.

EU: Article 43(2) provides internal-control conformity assessment for Annex III points 2–8; other assessment routes apply to specified systems, including applicable sectoral product-law routes (Art. 43(3)).

Decision: Stability over repeated runs and setups
EU: Consistency required by Arts 9(6), 15(1); no repeated-run statistic named there. Art. 15(2) provides for encouraging benchmarks and measurement methods.

UK: Use, output risk or uncertainty, and user-reported problems; guidance includes handover and reviewer-capability tests
EU: Risk and context shape oversight under Art. 14; use-specific biometric/text rules and data-protection limits apply in their respective scopes

UK: Rarely stated, and only in guidance (AI_Insights on benchmarks and uncertain cases; UK071 on when to override)
EU: Fact-checking for published AI text (Art. 50 guidelines); police uses (EU043); overseers of high-risk systems to stay aware of automation bias (Art. 14(4))

Decision: What the body learns about the tool
UK: ATRS record; model version may be left blank for off-the-shelf tools
EU: Instructions for use declare accuracy levels and metrics (Arts 13, 15(3))

UK: Announced £10m regulator package; cited £21m NHS deployment example; training, advice, templates and expertise also identified. Actual capacity not measured.

Decision: Means for logging and consistency testing
UK: No dedicated funding identified in the cited passages; guidance points to a free evaluation framework (Inspect, UK071)
EU: High-risk logging duties coexist with UK consistency-testing guidance, including repeatability and version-comparison methods (UK071; UK268). Actual resource sufficiency is not established.

UK: The body that uses the tool, even if bought in
EU: The deployer is responsible for its use; under the AI Act the provider answers for the system’s conformity, and the EDPS treats responsibility for an output as depending on its origin

UK: Public ATRS records and challenge routes coexist with existing legal/regulatory accountability
EU: Supervisor notifications/documentation coexist with public database information and scoped complaint/explanation rights

UK: Rarely stated; DWP discipline, Ofgem penalties, Equality Act legal action
EU: Member States set the extent of public-body fines; Union institutions have a separate fines regime. Art. 111(2) contains a scoped transition provision for relevant existing high-risk systems, not all public-sector AI.
